welcomeHelp.what: The way into the workbench. Every folder you open becomes a tab of its own, with its files, its editor and its chat with Claude side by side. Only folders under the roots this installation allows can be opened. Until each moves to a screen of its own, the round trip of the connection and your approved devices are below.
welcomeHelp.states: Recent folders come first, pinned ones on top. A folder marked as unavailable left the allowlist or the disk: it stays listed so you know why, and it cannot be opened. With no recent folder yet the list says so, and the roots below are where to start. The roots are the allowlist — the only folders this installation lets Claude work in. To allow another, run the command shown under them on the machine the backend runs on: the web never changes the allowlist.
welcomeHelp.notRecorded: Opening a folder records it among your recent folders and your tabs, on the server, so they follow you to another device. Nothing inside a folder is read to list it here, and the roots cannot be changed from this screen: that takes the pnpm allowlist command on the machine.

help.what: The trail of every tool Claude asked to run, and how each was decided: by a rule you granted, by a person, or by nobody in time. The filters live in the address, so a filtered trail is a link you can keep or share.
help.states: An entry a rule decided opens that rule, even after it was revoked. An entry nobody answered in time was refused. Loading more adds the next page; a failure there keeps what is already on screen, with the reason beside it.
help.notRecorded: The trail keeps the exact input of each tool, never the content of a file a tool read: for a read it keeps the path and the size. It records decisions, not the conversation.

screen.title: Devices
screen.purpose: The phones that may answer Claude's questions, and the ones waiting for your approval.

help.what: A phone with the app signs in and appears here, waiting. Once you approve it, it gets a push when Claude asks for permission, and can answer — allow or refuse — from wherever you are. A phone never approves itself: only a browser where you are already signed in can.
help.states: Waiting for approval: signed in, not allowed to answer yet. Approved: it receives the questions and may answer them. Revoked: it stopped answering at once, and its connections were closed; to use it again, sign in on it again. “No push token” means the phone only hears a question while the app is open.
help.notRecorded: Approving and revoking are recorded in the audit, with who did it and when. The screen does not show what a phone answered — that is in the audit trail, entry by entry.

help.what: Every rule you granted from a permission request: which tool, which pattern, where it applies and until when. Revoking is one click, and the next matching request asks you again.
help.states: An active rule answers requests without asking. A rule close to expiring — less than seven days left — is marked. An expired rule stays listed, marked as such; a revoked one leaves the list. A revocation that fails keeps the row, with the reason beside it.
help.notRecorded: Rules that only last a session are not listed: they end with it. This screen does not show which requests a rule answered — the audit trail does.

detailHelp.what: One rule, opened from the audit trail or from the list: what it allows, where, since when and until when.
detailHelp.states: Active, with the way to revoke it; expired; or revoked, saying when — never an empty page.
detailHelp.notRecorded: It does not list the requests the rule answered; the audit trail does.

screen.title: Workbench
screen.purpose: A folder of this machine: its files, its editor and Claude, side by side.

help.what: Each tab is one folder of this machine, with everything about it: the files, the editor and the chat with Claude beside them. A session started here runs inside the folder of the tab, and nowhere else. Open another folder with “Open folder…” or the + of the tab bar; each one is a tab of its own.
help.states: Up to 8 folders can be open at once; to open another, close one first. Closing a tab never ends its Claude sessions — they keep running on the machine, and come back when you open the folder again. A tab whose folder left the allowlist, or the disk, opens as an error, and the other tabs carry on. A place still empty says what will live there.
help.notRecorded: Which folders are open, and their order, are kept on the server, so they follow you to another device. The layout of each tab — its sizes, the open panels — is kept only in this browser. What you say to Claude and what it answers is the session's, not the tab's; decisions on permissions go to the audit trail.

screen.title: Logs and diagnostics
screen.purpose: Whether this browser reaches the backend, and how long a round trip takes.

help.what: Where to look when something seems stuck. The connection shows whether this browser is talking to the backend right now; the round trip sends one command through every layer — the gateway, the rules, the database — and shows the answer and how long it took.
help.states: Connected means everything on screen is live. Reconnecting means the connection dropped and the app is trying again on its own, waiting a little longer each time: “Reconnect” tries now. When the server asked the app to slow down, the button waits as long as the server asked, and says so. A ping waiting for its answer shows as loading; a ping sent while the connection is down says so, with the way to reconnect.
help.notRecorded: Nothing here reads your conversations or files. A round trip is counted on the server, and nothing else is kept. The logs of the backend and of the app are not shown here yet.

ping.title: Round trip
ping.description: One command across every layer — the gateway, the use case, the rule, the database — and back as an event.
ping.empty: Send a ping to see the whole chain answer, and how long it takes.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: The one connection every screen of this browser shares with the backend.
connection.heldBack: The server asked this app to slow down. It reconnects on its own as soon as the server allows.

screen.title: Settings
screen.purpose: How this app looks on this device, and the folders it may open.

help.what: The settings of the app itself: its look — theme, language, density — and the folders it works in. Claude's own settings — the model, the permission mode, MCP servers — are not here: they have a screen of their own.
help.states: Every option shows its default, and “Restore default” when it is set to something else. Appearance changes at once and is kept on this device only, so your phone can look different from your desktop. The folders this installation allows are read only here: adding one takes a command on the machine the backend runs on, which the section shows ready to copy.
help.notRecorded: Appearance is kept only in this browser, never on the server. Recent folders are kept on the server, so they follow you to another device; removing one here removes it everywhere, and never touches the folder on disk.

appearance.themeDescription: The system's follows your operating system, even when it changes while the app is open.
appearance.languageDescription: The language of the interface on this device. Push notifications keep the language the phone registered with.
appearance.densityDescription: Compact fits more on the screen, as a code editor does; comfortable has taller rows and larger text.

help.states: A version the backend could not read says why: not installed, or installed but unreadable. When the backend cannot be reached, only this web's version is shown, with the way to try again.
help.notRecorded: Reading the versions records nothing. Copying puts the block on your clipboard and nowhere else.
